candidates.change_summary: Change the require precondition from requiring at least one recipient to requiring exactly one recipient, so any multi-recipient call that completed in P now reverts and no longer returns true.
Replace the transferFrom function selector with a different selector, so the external call invokes an unintended function and the observable success/failure behavior changes.
Change the loop initialization from i = 0 to i = 1, so the first recipient is skipped and a different set of external calls is made.
Change the loop condition from i < _tos.length to i <= _tos.length, causing an extra external call with an out-of-bounds recipient and likely a revert instead of a successful true return.
Change the loop increment from i++ to i = i + 2, so every other recipient is skipped and fewer/different external calls are made.
Replace the per-recipient token amount v with a fixed 0, so each transferFrom is called with amount zero instead of v and the callee's behavior differs.
Remove the external call success check and its revert, so a failed transferFrom no longer reverts and transfer may return true where P would revert.
Change the external call recipient from _tos[i] to from, so all transfers target the same address instead of each recipient.
Change the final return value from true to false, so every successful call returns false instead of true.
Replace the revert() statement with require(false), which consumes all remaining gas instead of preserving it.
Change the require condition from _tos.length > 0 to _tos.length == 0, inverting the empty array check so the function reverts only when array is non-empty.
Delete the require(_tos.length > 0) statement, allowing calls with an empty array to succeed and return true without any transfers.
Delete the entire revert() statement inside the if block, so failed calls are silently ignored and execution continues.
Replace return true with return false, changing the success indicator returned to the caller.
Remove the loop by deleting the for statement, so no transfers occur and the function always returns true immediately after the require check.
